question: What should come in the place of blank number **3?**
solution:
The correct answer is '**Vivid**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence describes the vocabulary as "old-fashioned, but impossibly (3) _________." The word "but" indicates a contrast to the potentially "dry" nature of old-fashioned language.
 
• The crucial clue follows immediately: "...describing **gaudy pictures in my head** that were **more real than the creaky aisles**." This suggests the words created very clear, intense mental images.
 
• "**Vivid**" (ज्वलंत/सुस्पष्ट) means producing powerful feelings or strong, clear images in the mind. This perfectly fits the description of the reading experience being more "real" than the physical surroundings.
 
• "**Engaging**" (Option 1) means charming or attractive, but it doesn't specifically address the ability to create "pictures in the head."
 
• "**Simplistic**" (Option 3) and "**Unclear**" (Option 4) are negative or neutral terms that contradict the narrator's sense of being "amazed" and "whisked off" to another world.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

Complete Passage Segment: *The used bookstore was not merely a location where one might purchase books; it was a refuge. The air was thick with the earthy, rich smell of paper and dust, an odd fragrance which was at once soothing and (1) overwhelming__. I would spend hours there, running my fingers over the spines of ancient, forgotten books that stood on the shelves. Each novel was another world to discover, and I finally removed a leather-bound book with an odd, yellowed title. Its pages were dry and (2)__fragile__ . to the touch, as if one careless turn would make them disintegrate. As I picked up to read the opening lines, the words didn't merely speak a tale-they whisked me off to a whole different world, a place of magical creatures, gallant heroes, and secret spells. The vocabulary was old-fashioned, but impossibly (3)__vivid__, describing gaudy pictures in my head that were more real than the creaky aisles surrounding me. I was amazed by the imagination of the writer, a well that was presumably truly (4)_________. I felt a rush of awe, an appreciation that these tales, as ancient as they were, remained supremely (5) _________ and capable of igniting the imagination of a new generation.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Gaudy (भड़कीला):** Extravagantly bright or showy, typically so as to be tasteless. However, in this context, it emphasizes the brightness and intensity of the mental imagery.
 
• **Whisked off:** To take someone or something somewhere else very suddenly and quickly.
 
• **Imagery:** A literary device that refers to the use of figurative language to evoke a sensory experience or create a picture with words.
